PullRequest.Title: sessions: Open HTML files in integrated browser
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- use the Integrated Browser as the default editor for `*.html` files in the Agents Window on desktop
- keep HTML diff editors on their existing default
- add regression coverage for the Agents Window editor association defaults

Fixes #330412

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- `node --experimental-strip-types build\hygiene.ts src\vs\workbench\services\editor\common\editorResolverService.ts src\vs\workbench\services\editor\test\browser\editorResolverService.test.ts`
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\services\editor\test\browser\editorResolverService.test.ts` (32 passing)

## Notes

`npm run hygiene` could not pass its package pre-check on Windows because `build/gulpfile.hygiene.ts` constructed `C:\C:\Code\...\remote\package.json`. The focused hygiene checks for both changed files passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents Window startup and dynamic editor-association registration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The static configuration registers immediately; the dynamic schema rebuild waits for installed extensions and runs after registration changes or the Markdown-default setting change. The changed helper performs constant-size object construction on this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Registered editor count controls the pre-existing dynamic schema rebuild; the diff adds one constant HTML association independent of that count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Dynamic registration events are already debounced; configuration-setting changes invoke one synchronous rebuild. The diff does not alter scheduling or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or remote lookup is involved. Static and dynamic defaults are reconstructed when their existing registration paths run.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that no meaningful startup regression is introduced because the changed work is constant and surrounding editor enumeration/re-registration is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: the added work is one platform boolean read and one object property assignment.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The startup/configuration path gains only constant-size in-process work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening a local HTML file in the desktop Agents Window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor resolution now selects workbench.editor.browser. Its factory creates a lazy BrowserEditorInput and immediately starts resolve; visible browser content depends on main-process browser-view creation and file URL navigation, although createEditorInput itself does not await page loading.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Proxy call to the main process getOrCreateBrowserView.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per newly created browser editor for a distinct HTML resource; same-resource opens are deduplicated while open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Without the new Agents Window HTML association, ordinary HTML opens resolved to the prior default text editor and did not call the browser-view main-process service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to create the browser model; started eagerly during editor resolution, with the editor able to show loading state while navigation continues.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Constructs an Electron WebContentsView and attaches it to the window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One native WebContentsView per distinct open HTML browser editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior default text-editor path did not allocate a WebContentsView.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the Integrated Browser can render the file.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Electron webContents loads the local file:// HTML document and any page-defined subresources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One top-level navigation per cold browser-editor open, plus subresource requests determined by the HTML page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior text editor read the source through the text-file/model path and did not execute the document or load its browser subresources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The preview is not usable until the document load makes progress; navigation is asynchronous relative to returning the editor input.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One native browser view per distinct concurrently open HTML resource. Reopening the same resource while its editor is open is deduplicated by singlePerResource; opening N distinct HTML files can create N views.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The normal single-file user action creates one view. There is no global limiter for distinct files, so an external multi-open request could create views concurrently, but the diff adds no collection loop or fan-out caller and each view is the requested preview renderer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold open creates a BrowserEditorInput, main-process view, and navigation. Warm same-resource opens reuse the existing editor while open. Closing disposes the model/native view; a later reopen creates a fresh view. Browser session state may be shared, but native views are not cached after close.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the changed routing and boundary creation; lower confidence that realistic cardinality makes it a regression rather than the inherent cost of the requested HTML preview behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: WebContents memory/startup cost and page subresource count vary by platform and document, and no changed caller establishes bulk opening as a normal Agents Window workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance bug. The heavier boundary is the intentional renderer needed for the new default preview, same-resource work is deduplicated, resources are disposed, and the diff introduces no realistic fan-out or redundant creation mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening HTML diff editors in the Agents Window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Diff resolution uses workbench.diffEditorAssociations, whose changed helper intentionally contains only the Markdown rule, so HTML diffs continue through their existing editor resolution path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One resolution per diff open; the number of files shown in the diff does not add browser views through this change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged from the pre-diff diff-editor path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No browser-view cache is reached by this change for HTML diffs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the separate diff-association helper and resolver's diff association selection.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the changed code.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The change explicitly avoids routing HTML diffs through Integrated Browser.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening HTML in a web-hosted Agents Window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The default helper checks isWeb and omits the Integrated Browser association, so web HTML opens remain on the existing editor path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant platform check during association construction; HTML-open cardinality does not reach browser-view creation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or browser-view service is reached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence because the changed condition directly gates the association on !isWeb.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Integrated Browser is unavailable in web and the new default is not registered there.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced startup/configuration, desktop HTML open, HTML diff, and web scenarios through editor resolution, main-process IPC, native WebContents creation, file navigation, reuse, concurrency, and disposal. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found; the only meaningful added cost is the intentional browser renderer required by the feature, bounded to distinct open HTML editors and cleaned up on close.
